lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: Four years. Two hundred pages. Nine substantive amendments, none of them tabled, because tabling requires a sponsor and I am staff.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: Article nine is the one. Everything else is procurement. Article nine cedes the instrument, and it does it in a sentence about data custody that runs to a hundred and forty words.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: I can get one thing onto the floor before the reading. One. Tell me which, because I have stopped being able to see it.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: It carried. I have been in this building eleven years and today is the first time anything I wrote survived a reading.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: And now I would like to know who you actually are, and I would like to come with you when you tell me.

choices.text: We change what already happened. Come and see.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: Two hundred and forty-eight years downstream and my clause is still in force. Every so often I would like a moment to sit with that.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: The record is public now. Every buyer, every price. I did not write that amendment, but I will spend the next decade defending it.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: The session collapsed, so there was no reading, so there was no amendment, so there was nothing to lose a vote on. People keep telling me that as though it is a comfort.

lines.speaker: mara_vesely
lines.text: It goes through by executive order in six months. Unamended, unread, and with my post abolished in the same instrument, which I will admit is a detail I did not see coming. Four years, and the last thing I drafted was a handover note.
